The definition field of the same row is read only to understand a route, never classified. Routes against the definition field (axis: routes): 15,718 have route text equal to it (the source audit finds 7,463 of them to be a whole meaning field, 8,167 a whole usage field, which is the King James rendering list, and 88 whose text several entries of one key share (two entries in 87 of them, three in 1)); 7,889 carry the store's cut flag and are one tagged gloss cut from a meaning field; 39 more are one tagged gloss of an entry whose meaning field holds exactly that one gloss with a few untagged words round it, the flag left empty. The source's own key to its signs: none found. The lane's copy of the source (Open Scriptures HebrewLexicon, HebrewStrong.xml, commit 21c9add13bc727d3a951361778e97e3ff7afd1ce) shows its structure only: a meaning field whose glosses are tagged and a usage field that holds the King James list; it carries no key to its signs (no schema file and no documentation file in the copy), so every shape whose meaning rests on a sign convention begins "unverified:". The route text names neither the field it came from nor the entry's Strong's number; the lane read both from the source file by audit, which is evidence about the source and no part of any test.

definitions.first_match: The comma shapes are tried for a comma in the order of this declaration; the first shape whose test holds names the comma, and no later shape is tried for it.
definitions.containers: A comma's container is the innermost bracket that encloses it, as the checker's own bracket stack finds it: top when no bracket encloses it, paren for a round bracket, bracket for a square bracket, angle for the pair of angle brackets, brace for the pair of curly brackets. Its depth is the number of brackets of any of these kinds that enclose it.
definitions.character_words: Whitespace is any character that JavaScript's regular-expression class backslash-s matches. A letter is any character with the Unicode property Letter; a capital letter is any character with the property Uppercase Letter; a number character is any character with the property Number. A digit is one of the ten characters 0 to 9. A hyphen is the character U+002D, a full stop is U+002E, an apostrophe is U+0027, a right single quotation mark is U+2019 and a double quotation mark is U+0022. A word is a maximal run of non-whitespace characters, unless a test says it is a run of letters. Text is compared exactly, character for character, unless a test says 'written in lowercase'.
definitions.unbalanced: Scan the characters of the whole route text from left to right with a stack. An opening ( [ < or { is pushed. A closing ) ] > or } pops the stack when the top of the stack is its own opening bracket (( for ), [ for ], < for >, { for }); when the stack is empty or its top is another opener, the text is unbalanced at once. At the end the text is also unbalanced when the stack is not empty.
definitions.stripped_text: The text with every round group (an opening round bracket, then any characters that include no round bracket, then a closing round bracket) and every square group (an opening square bracket, then any characters that include no square bracket, then a closing square bracket) replaced by the single character U+0001; the replacement is repeated on the result, each time over the whole result, until nothing changes.
definitions.closing_period: In a stripped_text, a full stop that directly follows a letter, a number character, U+0001, a closing round bracket or a closing square bracket, and that is directly followed by a whitespace character, by the end of the text, by an apostrophe, by a right single quotation mark or by a double quotation mark. The first closing_period of a text is the one that comes first, reading from the left.
definitions.list_route: A route text for which all three hold: its stripped_text has no comma that has a whitespace character directly before it, unless the first character after that comma that is not whitespace is a digit; its stripped_text has no semicolon that has a whitespace character directly before it; and the route text itself, not stripped, holds neither the four characters i, full stop, e, full stop nor the four characters e, full stop, g, full stop.
definitions.trailing_note: A route text that is a list_route and whose stripped_text has a closing_period, when its list tail satisfies all four conditions. The list tail is the part of the stripped_text after its first closing_period, from the character after that full stop to the end, with whitespace removed at both ends. The four conditions: the list tail is not empty; it is not one run of one or more letters, apostrophes (U+0027) and hyphens followed directly by one full stop and nothing else (the last rendering, written after a full stop where a comma would stand); it is not one lowercase letter and nothing else (a lowercase letter is any character with the Unicode property Lowercase Letter; such a letter is a stray letter of the source's text and no remark); and it does not begin with the word See or the word Compare, each written with a capital first letter and followed by a character that is not one of A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9 or the underscore, or followed by nothing.
definitions.irregular_piece: Take the stripped_text of the route text up to and including the full stop of its first closing_period (a route text with no closing_period has no irregular_piece) and cut it at every comma. A piece is irregular when it is empty or holds only whitespace, the signs for multiplication (U+00D7) and plus, the character U+0001 and full stops; or when its first character that is not whitespace is a hyphen; or when it is not the last piece and its last character that is not whitespace is a full stop.
definitions.name_series: A text that, from its first character to its last, is one name or several names. A name is a capital letter followed by any number of letters, apostrophes, right single quotation marks and hyphens, and then, optionally, after optional whitespace, one round group that has no round bracket inside it. Between two names stand optional whitespace, then a comma or the lowercase word or, then optional whitespace.
definitions.list_comma: A comma of container top that satisfies the test of comma.between_renderings_in_semicolon_list, or the test of comma.between_kjv_renderings, or the test of comma.in_long_list_without_final_period, each of those three tests read by itself as if no shape stood above it.
definitions.label_last_piece: A route text whose stripped_text, cut at its last comma, has a last piece (the part after that comma, or the whole stripped_text when it has no comma) that begins with a grammar label: remove from the start of the last piece every whitespace character and every U+0001 character; the first word of what is left is its first maximal run of letters (here a letter is any character with the Unicode property Letter), empty if what is left does not begin with a letter; the last piece begins with a grammar label when that first word is exactly equal to one of the grammar_labels (compared exactly, in lowercase).
definitions.opening_flagged_piece: The opening flagged piece before a comma of container top is found in these steps, or there is none. Take the text before the comma. Replace every round group and every square group in it by U+0001, exactly as stripped_text does (the replacement applied to that text alone). If the result holds a semicolon, keep the part after the last semicolon; otherwise keep all of it. If what is kept holds a comma there is no opening flagged piece. Otherwise remove the whitespace at both ends of what is kept; if the result starts with a flag (flag_start) it is the opening flagged piece, and if not there is none.
definitions.flag_start: A text starts with a flag in these steps. Remove the whitespace (as defined in character_words) at the start of the text. Then, as long as the next character is U+0001 (a round or square group of a stripped_text), remove it together with the whitespace that follows it (possibly none). The text starts with a flag when the next character is then the multiplication sign (U+00D7) or the plus sign (U+002B); a text with no character left, or with any other character next, does not.
definitions.unbalanced text: Read the characters of a text from the first. Each opening round, square, angle or curly bracket is pushed on a stack. Each closing round, square, angle or curly bracket is matched with the top of the stack: if the stack is not empty and its top is the opening bracket of the same kind, the top is removed; otherwise the text is unbalanced. The text is also unbalanced when the stack is not empty after the last character. (This is the ask's own helper unbalanced.)
definitions.pieces of a text: Read the text from the first character with a bracket count that starts at zero: add one at each opening round, square, angle or curly bracket, and at each closing round, square, angle or curly bracket subtract one, never going below zero. A semicolon is outside the brackets when the count is zero at it. Cut the text at every semicolon outside the brackets and drop those semicolons: the stretches between them (the first from the start of the text, the last to its end) are the pieces, so a text with n such semicolons has n plus 1 pieces.
definitions.piece after the mark: For a semicolon outside the brackets, the piece (see pieces of a text) that begins just after it.
definitions.piece before the mark: For a semicolon outside the brackets, the piece (see pieces of a text) that ends just before it.
definitions.kind of a piece: Take the lead of the piece, which is the piece with its leading whitespace removed and, if what remains begins with an opening round bracket, that one bracket character removed as well; the first word of the lead is the first maximal run of letters (a letter is any letter of any script) at the very start of the lead, or the empty word if the lead does not begin with a letter. The kind is the first of these that applies, in this order: restatement, when the lead begins with the letter i, a period and the letter e, or with the letter e, a period and the letter g, in either case not followed by a letter, or begins with the words that is or the word namely, not followed by a letter; name description, when the lead begins with the words the name, the words the designation or the words also of, each with single spaces and not followed by a letter; also, when the first word is in also words; hence, when it is in hence words; transfer, when it is in transfer words; figurative, when it is in figurative words; narrowing, when it is in narrowing words; named use, when the first word is in named-use words, or when the first word is the word in and the lead begins with in, a space, a, a space and a word that is in in-sense words; alternative, when it is in alternative words; plain, when it is in plain-opener words; note, when it is in usage-note words; bracketed, when the piece with its leading whitespace removed begins with an opening round bracket; otherwise other. Every word list matches case-sensitively and in lowercase only.
definitions.head word of its own: A piece has a head word of its own when the following leaves at least one maximal run of letters that is not in label words: take the piece with every bracket character and every character read at a bracket count above zero removed (counting as in pieces of a text); then remove each occurrence of the word by, that is, each maximal run of letters equal to by that is preceded by the start of the text or by a non-letter, together with the whitespace after it and the maximal run of letters after that when both exist (a by with nothing after it is removed alone).
definitions.cuts cleanly: A text cuts cleanly when it has at least two pieces, every piece has a head word of its own, and every piece after the first has a kind that is in boundary kinds.
definitions.stands alone: A piece stands alone, or not, by these steps. The outside words of a piece are the maximal runs of letters (a letter is any letter of any script), in order from the left, of the piece after every bracket character and every character read at a bracket count above zero have been removed (counting as in pieces of a text); the whole-piece words of a piece are the maximal runs of letters of the piece with nothing removed. Step 1, for a piece that is not the first piece of its text: it does not stand alone if one of its outside words is in pronoun words, or one of its whole-piece words is in back words, or its lead (see kind of a piece) begins with the letters in, one space, the letter a or the letters an, one space, one or more letters, one space and the letters one, not followed by a letter. Step 2, for every piece: put a count at 2 if the first outside word is by or as, and at 0 otherwise; while the outside word at that count (counting from 0) exists and is in front words, add 1 to the count; the piece does not stand alone if no outside word is left at that count, or if the outside word there is in non-opening words. Otherwise the piece stands alone. Every word list matches case-sensitively and in lowercase only.
definitions.all pieces stand alone: A text's pieces all stand alone when every piece of the text (see pieces of a text) stands alone, the first piece being tested as the first piece of its text and every other piece as a piece that is not the first.
definitions.front words: A word is in front words when it is in label words and is not the word as, and also when it is one of the three words and, probably and perhaps, which label words does not hold. No other word is in front words. The list matches case-sensitively and in lowercase only.
definitions.looks like a King James list: The text with its trailing whitespace removed ends with a period, and no whitespace character stands directly before a comma anywhere in the text.
definitions.later pieces unlabelled: The text has at least two pieces and every piece after the first has the kind other.
definitions.word before the mark: Take the text before the mark, remove its trailing whitespace, and take the maximal run of letters that ends it; the empty word if it does not end with a letter.
definitions.dots of ie: A period is a dot of ie when the text before it ends with the letter i, itself preceded by the start of the text or by a non-letter, and the text after it begins with the letter e not followed by a letter; or when the text before it ends with the letter i, a period and the letter e, with that i preceded by the start of the text or by a non-letter.
definitions.dots of eg: A period is a dot of eg when the text before it ends with the letter e, itself preceded by the start of the text or by a non-letter, and the text after it begins with the letter g not followed by a letter; or when the text before it ends with the letter e, a period and the letter g, with that e preceded by the start of the text or by a non-letter.
definitions.run of dots: The character just before the mark is a period, or the character just after it is a period.
definitions.starts with a pointer word: The text after the mark, with its leading whitespace removed, begins with a word that is in pointer words and is not followed by a letter.
definitions.paren_first_match: The shapes of a mark are tried in the order of this declaration; the first shape whose test holds names the mark, and no later shape is tried for it.
definitions.paren_pairing: Scan the whole route text from left to right with a stack of opening brackets. An opening bracket ( [ < or { is pushed. A closing bracket ) ] > or } pairs with the opening bracket on top of the stack when that opening bracket is its own kind (( for ), [ for ], < for >, { for }), and that opening bracket is then taken off the stack; otherwise the closing bracket pairs with nothing and the stack is left as it was. At the end, each opening bracket still on the stack pairs with nothing. The group of a pair is the text strictly between its opening bracket and its closing bracket (it may be empty, hold whitespace, or hold other brackets); the group of a closing bracket is the group of its pair; an opening bracket that pairs with nothing has no group, and neither has a closing bracket that pairs with nothing.
definitions.paren_container: The container of a mark, as the checker's own bracket stack finds it: a pair encloses a mark when the mark lies between its opening and its closing bracket (an opening bracket that pairs with nothing encloses nothing, so a mark after it is not enclosed by it). The container is top when no pair encloses the mark; otherwise it is paren when the innermost enclosing pair is round, bracket when it is square, angle when it is angle, brace when it is curly. A bracket character sits in what encloses its pair, not in its own pair.
definitions.paren_character_words: Whitespace is any character that the JavaScript regular-expression class backslash-s matches. A letter is any character with the Unicode property Letter. A number character is any character with the Unicode property Number. A mark character is any character with the Unicode property Mark. A digit is one of the ten characters 0 to 9. A hyphen is the character U+002D. The multiplication sign is the character U+00D7. An apostrophe is the character U+0027 or the character U+2019 (the right single quotation mark). Text is compared exactly, character for character, upper and lower case being different; every word list below is written in lowercase and matches lowercase only.
definitions.paren_one_word_group: A group is one word when, with the whitespace at both ends removed, it is one or more characters and each of them is a letter, a mark character, a hyphen or an apostrophe (paren_character_words).
definitions.paren_against_letter: A round group stands against a letter when the character directly before its opening bracket (the opening bracket of its pair) is a letter (paren_character_words); a group at the very start of the text, and a group that has whitespace or any other character that is not a letter directly before its opening bracket, does not.
definitions.paren_runs: The runs of a group are its maximal stretches of consecutive characters that are each a letter or a number character, in order from the left; the first run is the first word of the group. The lead of a group is its runs joined by single spaces. A lead begins with a list item when the lead with one space added at its end begins with the item followed by one space.
definitions.top_level: A mark sits at top_level when no bracket pair encloses it, by the template's own bracket matching (round, square, angle and curly brackets; an opening bracket that never closes encloses nothing); a bracket character sits in what encloses it, so a pair of square brackets that no other bracket encloses has both of its characters at top_level. For such a mark the template's c.container is top.
definitions.square_bracket_container: A mark sits inside square brackets when the innermost bracket pair that encloses it, by the template's own bracket matching, is a pair of square brackets (the template's c.container is bracket).
definitions.letter: Any character with the Unicode property Letter, Hebrew letters and Latin letters included; a digit, a whitespace character and a mark are not letters. Lowercase s means the character U+0073 only; Doubtful is written with an uppercase D (U+0044) and lowercase letters.
definitions.whitespace: Any character that the regular-expression class backslash-s matches.
definitions.neighbours: The character directly before a mark is the one just before it in the route text and the character directly after it is the one just after it; at the start or the end of the route text that neighbour is missing, and a missing neighbour is not a letter, is not whitespace and equals no listed character. The two characters directly before a mark are the last two characters of the text before it (fewer if the text before it is shorter).
definitions.unpaired_apostrophes_before: The number of apostrophes (U+0027) that stand before the mark in the route text, not counting an apostrophe that has a letter directly before it and a letter directly after it (both neighbours taken from the whole route text).
definitions.bracket_group: For an opening or a closing square bracket that the template's bracket matching pairs with its partner, the text between the two brackets (neither bracket included); the closing bracket sits at the end of the text before it, so for a closing bracket the text before it is its opening bracket followed by that group exactly when the opening bracket is the first character of the route text.

shapes.means: separates the words of a parenthetical note or pointer that the source's usage field adds after the full stop closing its list of renderings (9 of 9 in the usage field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; the route text is a list_route; and the stripped_text of the text before the round group that holds the comma (the stripping applied to that text alone) holds a closing_period. The round group that holds the comma starts at the nearest opening round bracket before the comma that has not been closed before the comma, counting round brackets only.

shapes.means: unverified: separates words that may stand in the same place inside a parenthesis of a rendering in the usage list, each one completing the rendering around the parenthesis (918 of 918 in the usage field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; the route text is a list_route; and the stripped_text of the whole route text holds a closing_period.

shapes.means: unverified: follows a label word (causatively, figuratively, specifically and the others of the list) that opens a clause of an aside in a definition (122 of 122 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; and the text inside the round group that holds the comma, from just after its opening round bracket to the comma, taken after its last semicolon (all of it when it has none), with the whitespace at both ends removed and written in lowercase, is equal to one of the adverb_openers. The round group that holds the comma is found as in the test of comma.paren_in_note_after_list.

shapes.means: ends the wording that an i.e. restatement explains inside a parenthetical aside of a definition (26 of 26 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; and the text after the comma begins, after any whitespace, with the four characters i, full stop, e, full stop.

shapes.means: closes a run of examples inside a parenthetical aside of a definition by introducing the abbreviation that ends the run (37 of 37 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; and the text after the comma begins, after any whitespace, with the four characters e, t, c, full stop.

shapes.means: unverified: brings an alternative, an addition or a qualification into a parenthetical aside of a definition with a joining word of the list (86 of 86 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; and the text after the comma begins, after any whitespace, with a letter, and the first maximal run of letters of that text (the longest run of consecutive letters that starts at that letter, a letter being any letter of any script) is, written in lowercase, equal to one of the joining_words.

shapes.means: follows a word or number that the source marks with its own tag inside a parenthetical aside of a definition, the end of the tag leaving a space before the comma; it joins that gloss to a second gloss or a clause of the aside (108 of 108 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; and the character directly before the comma is a whitespace character (character_words).

shapes.means: general: any other comma inside the parentheses of a definition, with no tag space before it; it joins the items or clauses of one aside, and of the commas read in it about 3 in a hundred open an infinitive clause, 13 a phrase led by a, an or the, between 6 and 13 a phrase led by a preposition, between 5 and 9 a label word (each end of these two ranges is a count made with a different word list), and the other 62 to 73 a further word, item or phrase (350 of 350 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is paren; any other comma in parentheses: every comma of container paren that no shape listed before this one has taken.

shapes.means: follows a word that the source marks with its own tag inside a square-bracket note of a definition, the end of the tag leaving a space before the comma; it lists the items of the note (3 of 3 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is bracket (the innermost bracket is a square bracket); and the character directly before the comma is a whitespace character (character_words).

shapes.means: unverified: introduces a correction inside a square-bracket note of a definition: the source gives a number it takes to be wrong and, after the comma, the number it corrects it to (1 of 1 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is bracket; and the text after the comma begins, after any whitespace, with the word corrected in lowercase, followed by a character that is not one of A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9 or the underscore, or followed by nothing.

shapes.means: general: any other comma in a square-bracket note of a definition; it joins two words of a phrase the source supplies in brackets (1 of 1 in the definition field).
shapes.test: first_match; the container is bracket; any other comma in square brackets: every comma of container bracket that no shape listed before this one has taken.

shapes.means: separates two sense groups of a definition in which a bracket was left open or closed without being opened, so the source's text is damaged there and the whole entry is kept as written (all thirteen occurrences are in the meaning field).
shapes.test: A semicolon, at top level or inside a bracket, in a text that is an unbalanced text (see unbalanced text); this shape stands first among the semicolon shapes and takes every semicolon of such a text.

shapes.means: ends a definition that stops after the mark with no further sense written, as the source file itself ends six of its meaning fields with a semicolon.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level after which nothing but whitespace follows to the end of the text.

shapes.means: general: any other top-level semicolon that does not stand between a word, a number or a bracket on each side; the one occurrence read, which is all the dictionary holds (1 of 1), follows a quoted gloss closed by a quotation mark and comes before a note on how the particle is joined to verbs, so no second gloss stands on that side.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level, not caught above, such that the text before it with trailing whitespace removed does not end with a letter, a digit, a closing round bracket, a closing square bracket, a question mark or an exclamation mark, or the text after it with leading whitespace removed does not begin with a letter, a digit, an opening round bracket or an opening square bracket (a letter is any letter of any script, a digit is any decimal digit).

shapes.means: separates the descriptions of different bearers of one name (a person, a place, a tribe) in an entry that begins with the name, about fifty-six of sixty opened by also, and gives the entry's own account of each bearer or form.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level in a text that, with its leading whitespace removed, begins with this: one uppercase letter (an uppercase letter of any script), then any number of letters, apostrophes, right single quotation marks (U+2019) and hyphens, then any number of further groups each made of whitespace, one uppercase letter and any number of letters, apostrophes, right single quotation marks and hyphens, then optional whitespace, and then a comma, a semicolon, a period, the letters o and r followed by one whitespace character, or an opening round bracket followed by the letters o and r with no letter after them.

shapes.means: introduces an i.e. restatement that explains the sense written before it, so the restatement belongs with that sense.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark (see piece after the mark) has the kind restatement (see kind of a piece).

shapes.means: introduces a qualification of how, how often or by whom the word is used, a note on the sense before it, which in a little over half of the 24 read also offers words as renderings, but only in the same piece as the usage word that opens it, so that the piece is a note as a whole and is held whole under every answer, a note being no reading.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind note (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in usage-note words).

shapes.means: introduces a sentence saying that the word is the name or the designation of something, or is used also of another bearer, a description that belongs to the name it describes.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind name description (see kind of a piece).

shapes.means: stands beside a piece made only of sense labels and bracketed words, where the gloss that the label announces is written in round brackets or is missing.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level for which the piece before the mark or the piece after the mark has no head word of its own (see head word of its own and label words).

shapes.means: separates two groups of King James renderings in the usage list of the entry (all of its occurrences are in the usage field), each group a set of renderings of the one Hebrew word.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind other, in a text that looks like a King James list (see looks like a King James list), whose later pieces are unlabelled (see later pieces unlabelled), and which does not have a trailing_note (see trailing_note).

shapes.means: general: introduces a further piece that begins with no sense label the ledger knows: about two in three a bare gloss or a gloss opened by a small word (with, of, once, probably, in, if), about one in seven a name with its description, about one in ten a continuation opened by and, and the rest a label the list lacks (interrogative, intransposed, properly); in the source's own file 34 of 36 come from the meaning field and 2 from usage lists that stay whole.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level, not caught above, whose piece after the mark has the kind other (see kind of a piece).

shapes.means: separates sense groups of a definition in which some group may lean on another, because it points back at another group (with it, its, itself, both, them, they, their, one, above, same, former or latter), or opens with a note word or a preposition that leaves it no head word of its own, so that a cut here could print a group that is no reading on its own, and the whole definition is held (all 59 occurrences are in the meaning field by the audit).
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level, in a text that cuts cleanly (see cuts cleanly) but whose pieces do not all stand alone (see all pieces stand alone, stands alone, pronoun words, back words, front words and non-opening words).

shapes.means: general: separates sense groups of a definition in which another semicolon is followed by a note, an unlabelled sense, a name or a label with no gloss, so that cutting here would leave a piece with a note or two readings; of the groups it separates about 71 in 100 open with also, by, figuratively, hence or specifically, about 18 in 100 with another sense label, and about 11 in 100 with a plain gloss opened by to, a, an or the.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level, not caught above, in a text that does not cut cleanly (see cuts cleanly, pieces of a text and boundary kinds).

shapes.means: opens the next sense group of a definition with also or likewise, adding a further sense of the same word.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind also (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in also words).
shapes.falsifier: A piece after this mark that is a note or a description of another bearer of a name, not a gloss of the word, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with hence, a sense that follows from the one written before it.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind hence (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in hence words).
shapes.falsifier: A hence piece that is a comment on the sense before it, with no gloss of its own, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with by and the name of the step that carries the sense over (implication, analogy, extension, resemblance and the others the entries use).
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind transfer (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in transfer words).
shapes.falsifier: A piece opened by by that is a note or a restatement, not a gloss of the word, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with figuratively, giving the figurative sense of the word.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind figurative (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in figurative words).
shapes.falsifier: A figuratively piece that carries no gloss of its own would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with specifically, especially or generally, a narrower or wider use of the word with a gloss of its own.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind narrowing (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in narrowing words).
shapes.falsifier: A piece opened by one of these words that restates the sense before it, with no gloss of its own, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with a label naming a use, role or field of the word (causatively, concretely, abstractly, as noun, adverbially, in a good sense and the other words of the list) followed by its gloss.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind named use (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in named-use words, or the lead begins with in a and a word of in-sense words).
shapes.falsifier: A piece opened by one of these labels that is a note on use, with no gloss, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with no label, a gloss that begins with to, a, an or the.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind plain (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in plain-opener words).
shapes.falsifier: A piece opened by one of these words that is a note about the word, or a description cut from a name, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with or, offering another rendering of the sense with a gloss of its own.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind alternative (see kind of a piece: the first word of its lead is in alternative words).
shapes.falsifier: A piece opened by or that offers a guess about the identity of a name, or has no gloss, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: opens the next sense group with a label in round brackets that is not one of the known sense labels (upward, in number, partially) followed by its gloss.
shapes.test: A semicolon at top level whose piece after the mark has the kind bracketed (see kind of a piece: the piece with leading whitespace removed begins with an opening round bracket).
shapes.falsifier: A piece that begins with a round bracket and is a note, a pointer or a number, not a gloss, would prove the shape wrong.

shapes.means: inside an aside in round brackets, separates parts of the aside where the next part opens with a sense label: by a hand count of every one of the 27 routes (axis: routes), the next part is another application of the word (a figurative, causative or other named use, an alternative or an added sense) in 21 routes, and in the other 6 it gives a condition of use, a reason for the sense or a note on the grammar of the word.
shapes.test: A semicolon inside round brackets whose text after the mark has a kind that is in paren label kinds (see kind of a piece, applied to the text after the mark).

shapes.means: general: separates the parts of an aside in round brackets, of which about 25 in 100 open with a word of number, frequency or use (often, plural, only, usually, or the source's misspelling of usually), about 14 in 100 with and or but, about 29 in 100 with the, of, in, from or also, and about 32 in 100 with another word, a further gloss, an application of the word or an explanation of the word before it.
shapes.test: A semicolon inside round brackets, not caught above.

shapes.means: closes an abbreviation, a restatement or the list of renderings in an entry whose brackets are damaged or unbalanced, so the whole entry is kept as written.
shapes.test: A period, at top level or inside a bracket, in a text that is an unbalanced text (see unbalanced text); this shape stands first among the period shapes and takes every period of such a text.

shapes.means: unverified: is one dot of a run of dots that stands for words left out of a King James rendering, as in a pattern of two renderings with a gap (about nine in ten in the usage field).
shapes.test: A period at top level that is in a run of dots (see run of dots).

shapes.means: is a dot of the abbreviation i.e., which the definition writes before a restatement of the sense (all 2,701 are in the meaning field).
shapes.test: A period at top level that is a dot of ie (see dots of ie).

shapes.means: is a dot of the abbreviation e.g., which the definition writes before an example of the sense (all eight are in the meaning field).
shapes.test: A period at top level that is a dot of eg (see dots of eg).

shapes.means: closes the field: the King James list of the usage field ends with a period in 8,612 of the 8,673 usage fields of the source file (the other 61 end without one), and a few meaning fields end with one; of the 8,208 occurrences (axis: occurrences) the audit finds 8,100 in routes that are a usage field, 29 in routes that are a meaning field and 79 in routes whose text several entries of one key share (two entries in 78 of them, three in 1), all of them usage fields.
shapes.test: A period at top level after which nothing but whitespace follows to the end of the text.

shapes.means: closes a clipped word of the definition (reflex, poet, card, correl, trans, Marg and the etc of an aside), not a sentence end.
shapes.test: A period at top level for which the word before the mark (see word before the mark) is in period abbreviations.

shapes.means: ends a name or a list of renderings just before a cross-reference to another entry introduced by Compare, Comp, See or Marg (all 260 are in the usage field).
shapes.test: A period at top level whose text after the mark starts with a pointer word (see starts with a pointer word and pointer words).

shapes.means: ends the list of renderings before a note in round or square brackets that the source adds about the entry (ten of ten in the usage field).
shapes.test: A period at top level whose text after the mark, with leading whitespace removed, begins with an opening round bracket or an opening square bracket.

shapes.means: stands where a comma would, just before an i.e. restatement, so the restatement belongs to the phrase before it.
shapes.test: A period at top level whose text after the mark, with leading whitespace removed, begins with the letter i, a period and the letter e, or with the letter e, a period and the letter g, in either case not followed by a letter.

shapes.means: unverified: ends a quoted pattern of name endings inside a note on related names, just before the closing quotation mark.
shapes.test: A period at top level whose text after the mark begins with the apostrophe character (U+0027).

shapes.means: unverified: closes the list of renderings in the usage field, which the source file itself continues with one or two stray lowercase letters (all twelve are in the usage field).
shapes.test: A period at top level whose text after the mark consists of optional whitespace, then one or two lowercase letters (any lowercase letter of any script), then optional whitespace, and nothing more.

shapes.means: unverified: stands where a comma would stand before the last rendering of a list, so that one more word and a final period follow (all three are in the usage field).
shapes.test: A period at top level whose text before the mark ends with a letter or a closing round bracket and whose text after the mark consists of whitespace, then one run of letters, apostrophes and hyphens, then a period, then optional whitespace, and nothing more (a letter is any letter of any script).

shapes.means: general: ends a list or a name, and a sentence that begins with a capital letter or a Hebrew letter follows: a note on use or origin in seven of nine cases, once a variant spelling before a pointer, and once a phrase cut in two (a hand count of all nine occurrences).
shapes.test: A period at top level, not caught above, whose text after the mark begins with whitespace followed by an uppercase letter of any script or a Hebrew letter.

shapes.means: closes something no other period shape names: four in nine a period standing where a semicolon was meant between two senses, two in nine a spelling variant named in a pointer note, and the rest one each a name before its description, a word cut short, and a period before a comma (a hand count of all nine occurrences).
shapes.test: A period at top level, not caught above.

shapes.means: unverified: is one dot of a run of dots inside a rendering in round brackets that stands for words left out (all fifty-one are in the usage field).
shapes.test: A period inside round brackets that is in a run of dots (see run of dots).

shapes.means: is a dot of the abbreviation i.e. inside an aside in round brackets, restating the word before it.
shapes.test: A period inside round brackets that is a dot of ie (see dots of ie).

shapes.means: is a dot of the abbreviation e.g. inside an aside in round brackets, introducing an example.
shapes.test: A period inside round brackets that is a dot of eg (see dots of eg).

shapes.means: closes a clipped word inside an aside in round brackets, most often etc, also reflex, includ, techn and phys.
shapes.test: A period inside round brackets for which the word before the mark (see word before the mark) is in period abbreviations.

shapes.means: ends an aside in round brackets with a full stop just before the closing bracket: after its last word or a number about three times in four, and after a clipped word such as subject or direct the rest.
shapes.test: A period inside round brackets whose text after the mark, with leading whitespace removed, begins with a closing round bracket.

shapes.means: closes something inside round brackets that no other shape names: once a period just before the pointer See inside a note, and once a stop standing where a comma was meant.
shapes.test: A period inside round brackets, not caught above.

shapes.means: closes the etc of a list of examples inside square brackets, in the definition of a word for hand.
shapes.test: A period inside square brackets for which the word before the mark (see word before the mark) is in period abbreviations.

shapes.means: general: any other period inside square brackets; the one occurrence found ends the short editorial note Doubtful that the source adds after a rendering, so that is the only kind read in it (all of the share).
shapes.test: A period inside square brackets, not caught above.

shapes.means: opens a round bracket whose partner never comes in the same text: the source's own text leaves the bracket unpaired, so everything after it in that text sits outside any group (19 occurrences by the audit: 13 in the usage field, 6 in the meaning field; none of them is in a gloss cut from a longer field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); and the opening bracket pairs with nothing (paren_pairing).

shapes.means: closes nothing: a closing round bracket with no opening bracket before it in the same text to pair with: either the source's own text has the stray bracket, or the route is a gloss cut from a longer field and the opener lies outside the cut (18 occurrences by the audit: 9 in the usage field, 4 in the meaning field, 5 in a single gloss cut from a meaning; 5 of them in a cut gloss).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); and the closing bracket pairs with nothing (paren_pairing).

shapes.means: unverified: opens a group that holds only a space, which the source's usage field writes in the King James list in the place of a rendering word that is understood but not printed (11 occurrences by the audit: 11 in the usage field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group is not empty and holds only whitespace.

shapes.means: unverified: closes a group that holds only a space, which the source's usage field writes in the King James list in the place of a rendering word that is understood but not printed (11 occurrences by the audit: 11 in the usage field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group is not empty and holds only whitespace.

shapes.means: unverified: opens a group that holds only a question mark, the source's sign that the word before the bracket is of doubtful identification (1 occurrence by the audit: 1 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group, with whitespace removed at both ends, is the single character question mark (U+003F).

shapes.means: unverified: closes a group that holds only a question mark, the source's sign that the word before the bracket is of doubtful identification (1 occurrence by the audit: 1 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group, with whitespace removed at both ends, is the single character question mark (U+003F).

shapes.means: unverified: opens a group that has another round bracket inside it: a note that carries its own note, or in the usage field letters set apart inside a word that is itself set apart (62 occurrences by the audit: 50 in the usage field, 12 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a round opening bracket (U+0028).

shapes.means: unverified: closes a group that has another round bracket inside it: a note that carries its own note, or in the usage field letters set apart inside a word that is itself set apart (62 occurrences by the audit: 50 in the usage field, 12 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a round opening bracket (U+0028).

shapes.means: opens a group that has a square bracket inside it: a note that carries, in square brackets, an added word, a label, a comparison or a pointer to another entry (15 occurrences by the audit: 2 in the usage field, 13 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a square opening bracket (U+005B).

shapes.means: closes a group that has a square bracket inside it: a note that carries, in square brackets, an added word, a label, a comparison or a pointer to another entry (15 occurrences by the audit: 2 in the usage field, 13 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a square opening bracket (U+005B).

shapes.means: opens a group that holds a chapter and verse of Scripture: the source names the place where the word has the sense or the rendering it is explaining (21 occurrences by the audit: 12 in the usage field, 9 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a digit, directly followed by a colon (U+003A), directly followed by a digit.

shapes.means: closes a group that holds a chapter and verse of Scripture: the source names the place where the word has the sense or the rendering it is explaining (21 occurrences by the audit: 12 in the usage field, 9 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a digit, directly followed by a colon (U+003A), directly followed by a digit.

shapes.means: opens a group that holds a digit but no chapter and verse: in the source's file the number is a tagged link to another entry, so the group is a note that points to that entry, most often one saying that a rendering stands by mistake or by confusion for another word (43 occurrences by the audit: 37 in the usage field, 6 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a digit.

shapes.means: closes a group that holds a digit but no chapter and verse: in the source's file the number is a tagged link to another entry, so the group is a note that points to that entry, most often one saying that a rendering stands by mistake or by confusion for another word (43 occurrences by the audit: 37 in the usage field, 6 in the meaning field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a digit.

shapes.means: unverified: opens a group that holds the multiplication sign, the source's mark that the words after it are a rendering used only in a certain phrase, set inside an optional group of the King James list (45 occurrences by the audit: 45 in the usage field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds the multiplication sign (paren_character_words).

shapes.means: unverified: closes a group that holds the multiplication sign, the source's mark that the words after it are a rendering used only in a certain phrase, set inside an optional group of the King James list (45 occurrences by the audit: 45 in the usage field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds the multiplication sign (paren_character_words).

shapes.means: unverified: opens a group that holds the plus sign before a list of word endings, the source's mark that the endings are joined to the word beside the bracket as other forms of the rendering (1 occurrence by the audit: 1 in the usage field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the opening bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a plus sign (U+002B).

shapes.means: unverified: closes a group that holds the plus sign before a list of word endings, the source's mark that the endings are joined to the word beside the bracket as other forms of the rendering (1 occurrence by the audit: 1 in the usage field).
shapes.test: paren_first_match; the container is top (paren_container); the closing bracket pairs with its partner (paren_pairing); and the group holds a plus sign (U+002B).

shapes.means: opens a group that holds a word or phrase between single quotation marks: the source quotes the English word, the form or the saying that it compares or explains (7 occurrences by the audit: 7 in the meaning field).

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number. The source's own file gives every entry an id (H1, H2 and so on) that the store dropped, and the route text names neither the entry nor the field it came from; two entries under one letters key stand there as separate texts with nothing to tell them apart (example key בכרה: its entries in the source are H1072 and H1073, and its 5 route texts come from those two entries). keys_with_more_than_one_route_text counts senses and homonyms together. By the audit, of the 5,601 such keys (axis: keys; 5,939 letters keys in all) 4,182 are keys for which one single entry of the source file yields every distinct route text of the key (as its meaning, its usage or one of its glosses), and 1,419 are keys for which no single entry yields every text, so that the texts come from two or more entries that share the letters, true homonyms.

branches.question: The source ends each entry's usage field with the renderings the King James gave the word: one after another with commas between them, sometimes in groups with semicolons between the groups, and a full stop at the end (like: great(-ly); many, much). The route text does not say which field it came from, so the ledger knows such a list by its look, and that guess is why this waits for you. Does each comma and semicolon of such a list divide two readings, so that every rendering is its own reading and the list is cut at all of them at once? The next question (B02) is about the renderings marked with × or +.

options.means: Every comma and semicolon between two renderings of such a list divides, and so does the full stop that a few lists write where a comma should stand before the last rendering: every rendering, even a small word like and or or, is its own reading, and a pointer, a label or a stray letter after the last rendering stays in the last piece. The one exception is the commas that B02 asks about, the comma before a rendering marked with × or + and the comma after a marked rendering that opens a list or a group: they divide only if B02 says so. If it does not, a marked rendering stays joined to the rendering before it (to the one after it when it opens a list or a group), and renderings joined one after another in this way are printed together as one reading.
None of them divides: the list stays one reading, as one text. (B02 can still cut a marked rendering off the rendering before it, or off the one after it when it opens a list or a group.)

branches.question: Strong's marks some renderings of a usage list with a sign: × (a word the King James used only inside a phrase made with the Hebrew word) or + (a rendering made together with another word); the lane could not check the source's own account of the two signs. A sign alone is no reading, so the question is the comma beside it (like: age, × long, old). Is a rendering marked with a sign a reading of its own, cut off at the commas beside it and printed with its sign? It is meant for the case that B01 divides; if you keep B01 at whole and answer divides here, a list is still cut at the comma before each marked rendering, and after one that opens a list or a group.

options.means: A marked rendering is its own reading: it is cut off from the rendering before it (or, when it opens a list or a group, from the one after it), and when B01 also divides it is printed alone with its sign, whether it is a plain word, a small word like in or him, or a phrase; a pointer or a stray letter after the last rendering stays with it.
A marked rendering is not a reading of its own: it stays joined to the rendering before it or, when it opens a list or a group, to the rendering after it.

not_done_here: This ledger leaves to the route store the cutting of a definition into its tagged glosses and holds whole the commas that follow them (comma.after_tagged_gloss: of the occurrences read, about one in seven stands between a gloss and a qualifier, a label, a note or the description of a name, which the route text does not tell apart), so that of the 14,154 tagged glosses of the source's file (axis: glosses), which make 13,849 distinct key-and-gloss pairs (axis: pairs), the store serves 8,247 pairs as routes of their own and 5,602 pairs have no route of their own and so no pill here, and a pointer at the end of a text (See or Compare with a number) stays in the last piece.
